catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds a heater-off or safe-state action for a thermal.zone: cap.motion.stop.v1 binds robot.arm, robot.mobile_base and motion.axis, and cap.thermal.setpoint.v1 sets a target temperature instead of removing the heater demand. The action takes no input and writes SET:DEV:STILL_DB6.T1:TEMP:LOOP:HSET:0.0, the heater-loop command the clone exposes (Bluesky4/mercury_itc.py:81), as the SAFE-045 independent stop.

notes:
PASS on the fake backend: python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/kajalbiju__psi_bluesky_backend --backend fake exited 0 on its second run; G1-G9 all pass with no warnings. The evidence state is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. The package is model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run wC-095) and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached, no hardware backend was run, and no human review or hardware test is claimed.

Recon: all five card entry symbols exist in the clone: Bluesky4/SR830.py:9 (SR830), Bluesky4/mercury_itc.py:8 (MercuryITC), Bluesky4/sim928.py:6 (SIM928), Bluesky4/SR830_ophyd.py:5 (SR830Device) and Bluesky4/mercury_itc_ophyd.py:8 (MercuryITCController). This package binds one of them, MercuryITC; the SR830 lock-in and the SIM928 voltage source are separate devices in the same repository and are NOT COVERED, as are the ophyd wrappers and the Bluesky scripts.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's family-config/ScpiDriver is not used. The upstream builds each Mercury command from the fixed device address STILL_DB6.T1 (line 6) and a loop register (for example line 81), so a command table cannot reproduce the line; the package is a direct decorated Driver over Bluesky4.mercury_itc:MercuryITC with native.py. The wire syntax is unchanged: TSET is sent as SET:DEV:STILL_DB6.T1:TEMP:LOOP:TSET:<value>, exactly the line at mercury_itc.py:57.

Coverage: reads temperature (read_temperature), the temperature setpoint TSET (get_gas_flow), the heater setpoint HSET, and P, I and D; writes TSET, HSET and P, I and D. The safe-state action x-cap.kajalbiju.heater_off.v1 and the e-stop write HSET 0. NOT COVERED: the flow setpoint FSET (the clone has set_flow_setpoint but no getter, so exposing a write without a read would not be observable), the upstream set_gas_flow method (its follow-up query is a literal string containing {device_address} at line 59; the driver sends the same SET line through write and reads back with get_gas_flow), and the other devices named above.

Limits: no line of the clone states a range for TSET, HSET, P, I or D, so every numeric write is Limit.operator_required; nothing is clamped. site-limits.example.json is an illustrative operator overlay, not a statement of the device's own bounds. Units: temperature and TSET are K (the upstream strips a trailing K; read_temperature line 47 and get_gas_flow line 160), while HSET and P, I and D are declared unit '1' because the clone does not state their units.

Safety: the risk is R2 because the controller drives a heater (HSET). The clone documents no independent hardware e-stop and no heater-off method, so estop_physical_ref is not set; the SAFE-045 independent stop is the safe-state action writing HSET 0, and the @estop writes the same value. HSET 0 is the lowest heater-loop setpoint this driver can write; whether the unit treats it as heater-off is a device decision for the reviewer, not a sourced Fact. The loader refuses the hardware backend of an unreviewed model-written R2 package until reviewed_by is signed.

Fake: the card's preferred mock strategy is transcript, but the clone has no simulator, mock, upstream tests or recorded session. The fake is an in-package stateful stand-in implementing only upstream methods; every starting value is test data marked placeholder and the STAT: reply prefix is declared test data, and none of it is used as a Fact, a Limit or a reference. The gate and conformance suite call each read twice per action and the fake keeps state; there is no array to leave out.

Hardware backend: native.py adds the pinned clone's Bluesky4 directory to sys.path and constructs MercuryITC with the operator's visa_address. The upstream query and write open and close a PyVISA resource per call; the factory does not open one. The upstream query and write also catch VisaIOError and return None, so a VISA failure on hardware may surface as a missing or unchanged value rather than a failed receipt; the gate's failure injection exercises the fake path only. pyvisa is not installed by this package; the fake backend imports neither pyvisa nor the clone, and the hardware backend was not run.

License: the clone has no LICENSE file; the card is license_spdx NOASSERTION, license_class unknown. Publication needs the owner's decision (publish_review is required); no license is claimed.

Provenance: the clone was never modified and upstream code was never imported or run by this authoring session; only files under this package were written (plus check-report.json, which the gate regenerates and which is not part of the package). G4 and G8 produced no warnings; there are no PDF citations. gate.digest is the digest the last check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run.
